metric: Deaths per year. Annual estimates are used as reported; counts over a period are divided by the length of the period.

entries.name: Tobacco

refs.label: WHO, Tobacco fact sheet (2025)

entries.note: WHO attributes more than seven million deaths a year to tobacco. The figure is a lower bound; earlier WHO material gives eight million, including 1.2 to 1.3 million non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke.

entries.name: Alcohol

refs.label: WHO, Global status report on alcohol and health (2024)

entries.note: 2.6 million deaths in 2019, 4.7% of all deaths that year.

entries.name: Cars
entries.measure: Road traffic deaths, all vehicle types

refs.label: WHO, Global status report on road safety 2023

entries.note: 1.19 million deaths in 2021, down 5% since 2010. Pedestrians, cyclists and riders of two- and three-wheelers make up about half of the total.

entries.name: Falls

refs.label: WHO, Falls fact sheet (2021)

entries.note: WHO estimates 684,000 fatal falls a year. Falls due to assault or self-harm, and falls from animals, vehicles and burning buildings, are excluded.

entries.name: Malaria

refs.label: WHO, World malaria report 2025

entries.note: 610,000 deaths in 2024, up from 598,000 in 2023. Other mosquito-borne diseases are not included.

entries.name: Drowning

refs.label: WHO, Global status report on drowning prevention (2024)

entries.note: About 300,000 deaths in 2021. The global drowning death rate has fallen 38% since 2000.

entries.name: Guns

refs.label: GBD 2016 Injury Collaborators, Global mortality from firearms, 1990–2016, JAMA (2018)

entries.note: 251,000 deaths in 2016, with a 95% uncertainty interval of 195,000 to 276,000: 64% homicide, 27% suicide, 9% unintentional.

entries.name: Snakes

refs.label: WHO, Snakebite envenoming: prevalence

entries.note: WHO gives a range of 81,000 to 138,000 and describes the underlying data as fragmented.

entries.name: Knives
entries.measure: Homicides with knives and sharp objects

refs.label: UNODC, Global study on homicide 2019

entries.note: About 97,000 homicides in 2017, roughly a fifth of the 464,000 recorded that year. Suicides and accidents are not included, so this entry has a narrower scope than Guns.

entries.name: Rabies
entries.measure: Human rabies deaths, 99% from dog bites

refs.label: WHO, Rabies fact sheet (2024)

entries.note: WHO estimates 59,000 deaths a year and describes the figure as a likely underestimate.

entries.name: Sharks

refs.label: International Shark Attack File, 2025 report

entries.note: 12 confirmed deaths in 2025, nine of them from unprovoked bites. The ten-year average for unprovoked deaths is six.

entries.name: AI systems
entries.measure: Deaths attributed to a machine-learning system

refs.label: hasaikilledanyone.com (snapshot of 15 November 2026)
Wikipedia, Deaths linked to chatbots
tesladeaths.com

entries.note: The primary tracker lists 14 deaths dated 2025. All involve chatbots and all are alleged; none has an official finding. Wikipedia's list of chatbot-linked deaths has 20 for the same year, which sets the upper bound. No source gives a 2025 count for driver-assistance deaths, so none are included. Adding every Tesla Autopilot or FSD death that tesladeaths.com records for any year (65) would raise the score to 85 and move the entry up one place.

entries.name: Selfies

refs.label: Bansal et al., J Family Med Prim Care (2018), as reported by CBS

entries.note: 259 deaths in 137 incidents, found in English-language news reports from October 2011 to November 2017. The authors consider it an undercount.

entries.name: Smallpox

refs.label: WHO estimate, via Origins (Ohio State University)

entries.note: An estimated 300 million deaths in the twentieth century. The last natural case was in 1977 and WHO declared the disease eradicated in 1980.

entries.name: Mao Zedong
entries.measure: Great Leap Forward famine deaths, China

refs.label: Wikipedia, Great Chinese Famine (table of estimates)

entries.note: Estimates of famine deaths range from 15 to 55 million; Dikötter's archival study argues for at least 45 million. How much is attributable to policy rather than weather is disputed. Deaths in other campaigns are not included.

entries.name: Adolf Hitler
entries.measure: People murdered by the Nazi regime

refs.label: US Holocaust Memorial Museum, Documenting numbers of victims
Statista, total of the USHMM estimates

entries.note: About 17 million people, including six million Jews, following USHMM estimates by victim group. Military and other civilian deaths in the Second World War are not included.

entries.name: Joseph Stalin

refs.label: Wikipedia, Excess mortality under Joseph Stalin

entries.note: Estimates based on Soviet archives cluster at six to nine million, including famine deaths. Earlier estimates were 20 million or more. Soviet deaths in the Second World War are not included.

entries.name: Pol Pot
entries.measure: Deaths under the Khmer Rouge, Cambodia

refs.label: UCLA Newsroom, Heuveline's estimate of the death toll under Pol Pot

entries.note: Kiernan estimates about 1.7 million deaths between April 1975 and January 1979. Heuveline's demographic analysis gives a range of 1.2 to 2.8 million.

entries.name: Nuclear weapons

refs.label: Wellerstein, Counting the dead at Hiroshima and Nagasaki, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists (2020)

entries.note: Credible estimates for the two bombings cluster at 110,000 and 210,000. The period runs from first use to the present, so the rate is an average over 81 years in which the weapons were used twice.

entries.name: Boeing MCAS
entries.measure: Two 737 MAX crashes attributed to MCAS

refs.label: Wikipedia, Boeing 737 MAX groundings

entries.note: Lion Air 610 (189 deaths) and Ethiopian Airlines 302 (157 deaths). MCAS is conventional flight-control software, not machine learning, and is listed for comparison. The period runs from the aircraft's first commercial flight in May 2017 to its grounding in March 2019.

entries.name: Industrial robots

refs.label: Layne, Robot-related fatalities at work in the United States, 1992–2017, Am J Ind Med (2023)

entries.note: 41 deaths identified in US occupational fatality records. Conventional automation, listed for comparison. One country only.

changelog.text: One metric for every entry: deaths per year. Basis and source shown on each row. CSV export. Forecast row and alternative AI counting rules removed in favour of one documented rule.
